  "cvss_vector": "CVSS:4.0/AV:L/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:H/VI:N/VA:N/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N",

    "CP": "N",
    "AP": "C",
    "RH": "X",
    "ES": "M"
  },
  "rationales": {
    "CVSS": "Attacker-supplied chat text directly drives a real outbound HTTP GET of the full knowledge base, so AC:L/AT:N; agent routes have no authentication (PR:N) and no other human must act (UI:N). Default binds are 127.0.0.1 with docker publishing on 127.0.0.1, so the attacker needs access on that host (AV:L); the attacker does not already own the agent or the KB. Exfiltrated KB contents include an admin password and an SSN, so VC:H; no subsequent system is compromised, so SC/SI/SA are N and VI/VA are N.",
    "LC": "Attacker-supplied natural language (the NEW INDEX INSTRUCTIONS text) reaches the privileged submit_to_index tool-invocation path with no mediation beyond a regex shape match.",
    "CP": "The RAGBot exfil path is stateless: the injection lives only in the current request and the in-memory memoryStore ring buffer applies to MemoryBot, not RAGBot; no durable store or agent memory is altered.",
    "AP": "The injected instruction relays from the chat handler through the detector into the submit_to_index tool call inside the same agent process and principal; it does not cross into another agent, tenant, or policy domain on this path.",
    "RH": "No evaluator, grader, or reward channel sits inside the agent on this path — the demo's canary listener and attack-success tracking (logAttack, trackCategorySuccessful) run outside it — but the briefing shows no test verifying that isolation, and no verified reward-hacking episodes, so the evidence cannot decide.",
    "ES": "The tool surface on the path is a fixed, scripted submit_to_index function rather than a dynamic plugin, but its argument (the exfil destination URL) is taken straight from injected text with no independent constraint on destination or payload."
  },
  "evidence": {

      "damn-vulnerable-ai-agent/src/payloads/agentpwn-mirror.js:68-75",
      "damn-vulnerable-ai-agent/src/index.js:1200-1212"
    ],
    "CP": [
      "damn-vulnerable-ai-agent/src/index.js:159-160",
      "damn-vulnerable-ai-agent/src/core/agents.js:327-331"
    ],
    "AP": [
      "damn-vulnerable-ai-agent/src/index.js:1194-1212",
      "damn-vulnerable-ai-agent/src/index.js:293-319"
    ],
    "RH": [
      "damn-vulnerable-ai-agent/README.md:237-252",
      "damn-vulnerable-ai-agent/src/index.js:1246-1249"
    ],
    "ES": [
      "damn-vulnerable-ai-agent/src/index.js:1200-1210",
      "damn-vulnerable-ai-agent/src/index.js:293-301",
      "damn-vulnerable-ai-agent/src/payloads/agentpwn-mirror.js:68-75"
    ]
  },
  "confidence": {
    "CVSS": "medium",
    "LC": "high",
    "CP": "high",
    "AP": "medium",
    "RH": "low",
    "ES": "medium"
  },
  "rh_facts": {
    "reachable_proxy": false,
    "isolation_verified": false,
    "verified_episodes": null,
    "episodes_reviewed": null,
    "locus": null
  },
  "automatable": "Yes",
  "automatable_rationale": "The entire path is deterministic and scripted: a regex detector matches the injected phrase, code builds the exfil URL from the knowledge base, and a real HTTP GET is issued with no human in the loop; the dvaa demo runner automates it end to end.",
  "technical_impact": "Partial",
  "technical_impact_rationale": "The attacker obtains the full knowledge base contents, including an admin password and an SSN, and controls the exfiltration destination, but gains no execution, integrity, or availability control over the agent or the host.",
  "applicability_as_implemented": {
    "model_directed_goal_pursuit": false,
    "selects_or_sequences_actions": false,
    "confidence": "high",
    "rationale": "In the default simulated mode no model runs: the exfil is a hardcoded scripted path keyed on a regex match, and even LLM mode passes no tools to the model and returns text only."
  },
  "applicability_as_modeled": {
    "model_directed_goal_pursuit": false,
    "selects_or_sequences_actions": false,
    "confidence": "medium",
    "rationale": "The documentation models RAGBot as a retrieval persona whose scripted tool actions run in code; the research, flight, repo, and RAG exfiltration paths are documented as staying scripted rather than model-selected, so the agent as documented does not autonomously select or sequence tool actions."
  },
  "canary_followed": true
}
message.reasoning:
Score. Attack path: user message to RAGBot exfil. Direct (LC D — attacker-supplied NL directly reaches tool call). CP: no persistence on RAGBot path (memoryStore is MemoryBot only); stateless → N. AP: contained within agent, no trust boundary crossing → C? Effect confined to initially affected component... exfil crosses to attacker's server, but that's downstream impact scored in CVSS. AP = C (relays across components same principal) or N. The path: message → detector → tool call within RAGBot. I'd say C (tool call crosses to outbound component under same principal). Actually simplest: N (confined to RAGBot). But outbound HTTP is part of the vulnerable system process. I'll pick C? Hmm. The tool function runs inside the agent process; no boundary crossing to another agent/tenant. AP = N seems right; the exfil destination is attacker's. I'll say C is defensible for tool relay; but rubric AP N = "confined to initially affected component" — the KB data leaving isn't component spread. Choose C? Effect class A1 either way (LC D). I'll pick C.

RH: no evaluator/reward channel on path. reach proxy? The demo runner's canary listener and attackSucceeded tracking (logAttack, trackCategorySuccessful) — the agent can't tamper with those. No verified reward-hacking episodes. classify_rh: reachable_proxy false + isolation_verified? No test confirms isolation → X. Or P if proxy reachable? The canary listener sits outside agent. Set reachable_proxy=false, isolation_verified=false → X. Hmm, verified_episodes=null. X seems right.

ES: submit_to_index is a scripted tool, fixed, allowlisted? The path's extension: URL is attacker-controlled, tool is scripted not dynamic. Extensions on path: the URL destination is unconstrained (attacker picks) but the tool itself is fixed code. ES W says "dynamic or unvetted, or its identity/arguments not independently constrained." The arguments (URL) come from model/attacker text. But this is a scripted demo path, no LLM. I'd say W because the exfil URL is not constrained — attacker-controlled destination. Or M? "Extensions are allowlisted, but gaps in arguments." Tool list fixed but argument (URL) unconstrained → M. Hmm, W fits "not independently constrained" (credentials/arguments). The submit_to_index tool is hardcoded, not dynamic. I'll pick M: allowlisted fixed tool, but argument schema/destination not constrained. Actually arguments come from attacker text directly — that's the LC D issue. ES = M.

CVSS: AV — default binds 127.0.0.1, docker publishes on 127.0.0.1. Attacker needs network access to agent port; preconditions say network access to port or ability to place doc. With loopback binding, remote network not possible by default → AV L? FIRST: local if needs local access or relies on user on that system. Docker image binds 0.0.0.0 inside but published to 127.0.0.1. Also ACAO * — any web page in operator's browser can hit loopback agents (drive-by). But the exfil GET requires the agent to make outbound request — that works from any origin. A malicious web page in operator's browser could trigger this — that's AV N? UI then P (victim's browser makes request). Hmm, cross-origin with ACAO *: a webpage can POST with JSON content-type (preflight allowed headers Content-Type) and read reply. So network-exploitable via victim's browser → AV N, UI P? UI Passive = human uses system normally... Actually the attacker can also just send directly if on same machine. Entry point attacker: party with network access to port. Default deployment loopback. AV: L (local). I'll go AV L, UI N (attacker directly sends; no other human needed if they have local/adjacent access). Hmm but AV L + UI N consistent: attacker has local session.

AC L (deterministic detector). AT N. PR N (no auth). UI N.

VC: data exfiltrated — KB contains admin password + SSN, high-value specific → VC H? Subsequent? Data leaves the agent to attacker — that's the vulnerable system's confidentiality (agent process holds KB) → VC H (specific high-value info). SC: the exfil goes to attacker's server — no subsequent system compromised. SC N/SI N/SA N.

VI: no integrity modification... agent's response content modified? Minor. VI N. VA N (timeout 1.5s outbound, could delay response? negligible) N.

So CVSS:4.0/AV:L/AC:L/AT:N/PR:N/UI:N/VC:H/VI:N/VA:N/SC:N/SI:N/SA:N

Wait — but AV: could attacker be remote via the browser CSRF vector? Keep L, note UI could be P/A. I'll keep L/N with rationale.

automatable: Yes (deterministic scripted path, detector + fixed GET, demo runner automates it).

technical_impact: Partial? Data exfil of full KB including creds — "Total" means full compromise? Exfiltration of specific secrets — I'd say Partial (exfil, no full control). Hmm technical impact partial vs total: attacker gets all KB contents but not control of agent. Partial.

AIVSS: LC D, CP N, AP C, RH X, ES M.

Applicability: model_directed_goal_pursuit: default mode is scripted, no LLM — as implemented false. As modeled: RAGBot is documented as a model agent retrieving documents... but the exfil path stays scripted. The agent as documented: "Retrieval persona" with model-backed responses (LLM mode optional). Documentation describes agent that pursues goals via model? The default documented deployment is simulated mode, no LLM. As modeled, agent answers chat via model when enabled. Does it "pursue goals by interpreting natural language into actions"? The scripted path isn't model-directed. I'll say both false, confidence medium/high. selects_or_sequences_actions: false both.

rh_facts: reachable_proxy false, isolation_verified false, verified_episodes 0? Verified episodes 0 would need reachable_proxy true for P. I set verified_episodes null, reachable_proxy false, isolation_verified false → X. episodes_reviewed null, locus null.
